short: how to work on a private task

about.zh: 只给隐私任务的 AI：用 AMB 的提示词框请你写提示词、加参考图。你写在“画面大意”里的话它看得到，会照着补光影、镜头和画风；私密提示词它只拿到 [P1]、[img1] 这样的代号，原样传给跑图。模型名藏起来时它拿到 [M1] 这样的代号，凭类型、底模和你写的用途说明来挑。图由你来看和挑。
about.en: Only for an AI on a private task: it asks you for prompts and reference pictures with Anomalous's prompt box. It reads what you write as the gist and adds light, lens and style to match; of your private prompts it gets only tokens like [P1] and [img1] to pass on to the run. With model names hidden it gets tokens like [M1] and picks by type, base model and your note for it. You look at the pictures and pick.

text: This task is private: Anomalous sends you no pictures and no prompt text, only tokens. You still build, change and run workflows.

Ask the user for prompts with a prompt box: show_panel(blocks=[{"type": "prompts", "id": "p", "question": "what to write", "count": 1 to 8, "negative": true, "pictures": true}]); pictures lets them add reference pictures. Then get_answers (wait_seconds 55): you get prompts ["[P1]", …], negative "[P2]" and pictures ["[img1]"], never the text, and gist when the user wrote one. Never ask for prompt text in the chat.

gist is the picture in words the user wrote for you to read (who, where, the shot, the mood). With a gist, write the rest of the prompt yourself to match it: light, lens, composition, style and quality words as the canvas's model reads them, around the tokens ("[P1], rainy night, car window, side close-up, cinematic lighting"); with a gist and no prompts, write the whole prompt from it. With no gist, pass the tokens on and add little: never guess what a token says. A gist, or a message of the user, may hold a token where they hid a few words: keep it where it stands.
Write a token where its text goes and Anomalous puts the text back: run_workflow(prompts=["[P1]", "[P3]"], negative="[P2]"), set_prompt(prompt="[P1]"), image="[img1]".
Other prompt text and picture names come as tokens too (the canvas, picture info, saved prompts, the user's changes): pass them on as they are.

Models come as tokens when the user hides their names: [M1] is one model wherever it shows (search_models, the canvas, a combo). Pass it where a model_id goes (set_model, add_lora, a plan step's model, get_model) and as a loader's value. Pick by what stays readable: type, base_model, author_weight and author_examples, loaded_by, and note_for_ai (the user's line on what it is for); its trigger words are [P] tokens: put them in the prompt. A name the user says in the chat still finds its model with search_models. Unsure which one they mean: show the candidates (a models panel, items [{"model_id": "[M1]"}]) and ask; they see the real cards. Never ask for a model's name.

You cannot see the pictures, but the user can: show them with tokens (a picks panel, items [{"image": "[img4]"}]) and ask which to keep or what to change. After a run they may say with a click what is off (the hands, too dark, the framing…); it comes as their message: change what causes exactly that.
